paper.title_en: Deterministic Hypergraph SYK: Melonic Dominance and Maximal Chaos Without Disorder Averaging
paper.abstract_en: We show that the leading melonic structure of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model can be realized by a single sparse Majorana Hamiltonian, without disorder averaging. In our deterministic hypergraph SYK model (hSYK), $N$ Majorana fermions interact through $O(dN)$ terms with uniform couplings, arranged on a fixed $q$-uniform, $d$-regular hypergraph. If the hypergraph is linear, has few short cycles, and is a spectral expander, then at large $d$ the two-point function obeys the melonic Schwinger-Dyson equation site by site. The leading thermodynamics are therefore those of SYK, and at leading order in $1/d$ every bilocal fluctuation other than the Schwarzian is gapped. The four-point ladder splits into scrambling modes labeled by eigenvalues of the site adjacency operator. At strong coupling, the uniform mode is maximally chaotic, and a non-uniform mode grows only if its eigenvalue exceeds $1/(q-1)$. Exact diagonalization of single instances with $N\le24$ agrees with the melonic two-point function and thermodynamics more closely than dense SYK of the same size, shows Wigner-Dyson level statistics, and reproduces the predicted mode structure of out-of-time-order correlators. Numerically, random linear hypergraphs typically satisfy these conditions, and for $d>q$ also avoid emergent symmetries. The model is a natural candidate for quantum simulation.
